summary.text: Gregory W. Meeks is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 5th Congressional District. A lawyer and former Queens prosecutor, he served in the New York State Assembly from 1993 to 1998 before winning a 1998 special election to Congress; he represented NY-6 until 2013 and NY-5 since. He is the Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, which he chaired in the 117th Congress, and also sits on the Financial Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Meeks was born in East Harlem, New York City, in 1953, according to Wikipedia.
According to his official biography, his family came north from Rock Hill, South Carolina, during the Great Migration, and he grew up in a public housing project in East Harlem.
He earned a bachelor's degree in history from Adelphi University in 1975 and a law degree from Howard University in 1978.

Meeks served as an assistant district attorney of Queens County from 1978 to 1983, then as assistant special narcotics prosecutor of New York City, deputy counsel of a New York state investigation commission, and supervising judge of the New York workers' compensation board; his official biography describes him as chief administrative judge of the state's workers' compensation system.
He was elected to the New York State Assembly in 1992, representing the 31st District, and served until 1998.
Meeks won a 1998 special election to the U.S. House and represented New York's 6th District until 2013, then the redrawn 5th District.

On the Financial Services Committee he chaired its Subcommittee on Consumer Protection and Financial Institutions; his official biography says he was a Dodd-Frank conferee and co-authored several provisions of that law.
In the 117th Congress (2021–2023) he became the first Black member of Congress to chair the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and he is now its Ranking Member.
According to his official biography, he is a member of the New Democrat Coalition and co-chairs its Trade Task Force; Wikipedia also lists him as chair of the Queens County Democratic Party.
